question: By what authority and instrument does the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 come into force?
options: By notification of the Central Government in the Official Gazette
Automatically on the date of Presidential assent
By order of the Supreme Court
explanation: Section 1(2): it comes into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint — and different dates may be appointed for different provisions.

question: Which of the following is a NEW extraterritorial reach expressly stated in BNS Section 1?
options: Offences by foreign diplomats in India
Offences targeting a computer resource located in India
Offences on the high seas by any nationality
Offences committed in neighbouring countries only
explanation: Section 1(5)(c) applies the Sanhita to any person, anywhere beyond India, committing an offence targeting a computer resource located in India.

question: Under the general explanations, a child below what age can never commit an offence?
explanation: Nothing is an offence which is done by a child under seven years of age. A child aged 7-12 has only qualified immunity depending on maturity of understanding.

question: Section 2 of the BNS primarily contains—
options: The definitions of terms used in the Sanhita
explanation: Section 2 is the definitions clause, fixing the meaning of terms used throughout the code.

question: The Sanhita applies to an offence committed by a person on a ship or aircraft registered in India—
options: Only when it is within Indian territorial waters/airspace
Only if the person is an Indian citizen
explanation: Section 1(5)(b) applies to any person on any ship or aircraft registered in India wherever it may be.

question: Which of the following does Section 1's savings clause preserve?
options: Laws punishing mutiny/desertion in the armed forces, and special or local laws
Nothing — it repeals all prior laws
explanation: Section 1(6) states nothing in the Sanhita affects laws punishing mutiny and desertion of the armed forces, or any special or local law.

question: Under Section 2, up to what age is a person a "child"?
explanation: Section 2 defines "child" as any person below the age of eighteen years.

question: "Dishonestly" under Section 2 means doing an act with the intention of causing—
options: Wrongful gain to one person or wrongful loss to another
explanation: "Dishonestly" means doing an act with the intention of causing wrongful gain to one person or wrongful loss to another person.

question: Under Section 2, a thing is done in "good faith" only if it is done—
options: In the presence of a witness
explanation: Nothing is said to be done or believed in "good faith" which is done or believed without due care and attention. Mere honesty is not enough — reasonable care is required.

question: Under Section 2, "movable property" includes property of every description EXCEPT—
options: Land and things attached to the earth
explanation: "Movable property" includes property of every description except land and things attached to the earth or permanently fastened to anything attached to the earth.

question: Under Section 2, "person"—
options: Means only a natural living human being
Includes any company or association or body of persons, incorporated or not
explanation: "Person" includes any company or association or body of persons, whether incorporated or not.
